rounds.text: Sarda Proteins Ltd is trading at a discount to its intrinsic value, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 126 per share against the market price of Rs 97.8, offering a margin of safety of 22.3% [E36, E37]. The underlying business fundamentals have significantly outpaced recent stock performance, as evidenced by a 5-year profit growth of 102% dwarfs a share price growth of 19% [E13, E16, E47]. This strength is underpinned by excellent capital efficiency, demonstrated by a return on capital employed of 23.1% and a return on equity of 23.8% [E6, E7], both comfortably outperforming the sector medians of 10.2%, 16.7% profit growth, and 11.8% sales growth [E66, E67, E68]. Furthermore, promoters have displayed immense conviction by dramatically increasing their holding to 80.66% in June 2026 from 28.42% in September 2023 [E34], while the company remains virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.05x [E31, E50]. Technical momentum also supports the bull case, with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and holding a relative strength rating of 79 against the Nifty 500 [E41, E42]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 29.19x [E2], operating cash flow for March 2026 is negative at Rs -76.39 Cr [E28], and TTM sales growth has contracted by 48% [E11].

The valuation is aggressively extended, evidenced by a trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 31.6x and a staggering price-to-book ratio of 29.19x against a meager book value of ₹ 3.35 [E1, E2, E52]. Despite reporting profits, the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00%, offering no cash return to shareholders for this steep entry multiple [E4, E53]. Fundamental quality over medium horizons is also suspect, highlighted by a weak 3-year median return on equity of just 9% and a dismal 10-year median ROE of 2% [E19, E21, E54]. Operating performance has sharply deteriorated, with trailing twelve-month sales growth plunging by -48% and operating margins contracting to -14%, worsening by 2 percentage points over three years and crashing by 21 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E11, E23, E24]. Most alarming is the total collapse of cash generation, demonstrated by a catastrophic operating cash flow of -Rs 76.39 Cr and a free cash flow of -Rs 76.38 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -119.36x [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, reported earnings are inflated by non-operating sources, including Rs 5.83 Cr of other income [E55]. Conceded: [E34].

The valuation multiples of 31.6x P/E and 29.19x P/B [E1, E2] are fully justified because fundamentals are massively outpacing price action, with 5-year profit growth at 102% compared to a share price growth of just 19% [E16]. The lack of dividend [E4] reflects reinvestment, driving stellar profitability where ROCE and ROE sit at robust levels of 23.1% and 23.8% respectively [E6, E7]. While longer-term median ROEs look low historically [E19, E21], the last year's median ROE surged to 24% [E22], and rules-based screening confirms a strong 83/100 buy score [E56]. Conceded: [E23, E24, E28]. Although operating cash flow was negative in March 2026 [E28], the company remains almost debt-free with a minimal debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E31], and a discounted cash flow model explicitly demonstrates a 22.3% margin of safety against the current market price [E36, E37].

Conceded: [E16]. However, pointing to long-term profit growth ignores the alarming reality that trailing twelve-month sales growth has collapsed by -48% [E11]. The bull cites strong recent ROCE and ROE [E6, E7], but glosses over the fact that the median return on equity over 10 years sits at a paltry 2% [E19] and 9% over 3 years [E21], meaning the recent profitability spike is an outlier rather than a structural baseline. Conceded: [E31]. Despite being nearly debt-free, the company's operating cash flow plunged to an alarming negative Rs -76.39 Cr in March 2026 [E28], resulting in a catastrophic cash conversion of -119.36x [E27]. The assertion that valuation multiples are justified [E1, E2] ignores severe margin degradation, evidenced by quarterly operating margins plunging by -21 percentage points to -25% in June 2026 [E24]. Finally, leaning on a DCF model [E36] fails to offset the heavy baggage of a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -87.5% [E44].
